project.name: Routr
project.title: How much SIP traffic Routr handles.
project.lead: We run these tests after significant changes to the code, on dedicated DigitalOcean servers. Routr runs on one server and on Kubernetes; capacity tests find the limits, then both soak for 2 hours at half of them to catch leaks.

narrative.what: The EdgePort on its own, with Echo answering every request with 200 OK.
narrative.why: The EdgePort is the only stateful piece of Routr; this is its ceiling.
narrative.how: SIPp sends SIP MESSAGE over UDP, from 1,000 messages/s, adding 250 every 30 s, up to 10,000.

benchmarks.title: RoutrOne, simple calls

narrative.what: RoutrOne with the files backend, routing calls between 200 registered Agents. Every call is answered.
narrative.why: How many calls per second one server handles end to end, authentication included.
narrative.how: SIPp registers 200 callees, then ramps authenticated calls held 5 s over UDP, from 50 calls/s, adding 50 every 30 s, up to 3,000.

benchmarks.reason: load generator saturated at 2,900 calls/s (sipp-register at 85% of one core)

benchmarks.title: RoutrOne, the call mix

narrative.what: RoutrOne routing calls between 1,800 registered Agents, 60% answered, 15% busy, 15% cancelled and 10% to offline Agents.
narrative.why: Real traffic is not all answered calls; busy, cancelled and offline calls cost Routr work too.
narrative.how: SIPp registers 1,800 callees, then ramps the mix over UDP, answered calls held 5 s, from 50 calls/s, adding 50 every 30 s, up to 3,000.

benchmarks.reason: load generator saturated at 2,800 calls/s (sipp-register at 80% of one core)

benchmarks.title: Routr on Kubernetes, simple calls

narrative.what: The Connect chart, three EdgePorts behind a DigitalOcean Network Load Balancer, on three c-8 nodes, plus Dispatcher, Connect, Location (Redis) and the Data API (Postgres), routing calls between 200 registered Agents.
narrative.why: How a service-based deployment compares with one server, and what the load balancer costs.
narrative.how: SIPp registers 200 callees through the load balancer, then ramps authenticated calls held 5 s over TCP, from 50 calls/s, adding 50 every 30 s, up to 3,000.

benchmarks.reason: the results could not be analyzed: .perfkit/20261109T135040Z-71048a6/raw/k8s-simple: no SIPp -trace_stat file for one-soak/uac_invite.xml

narrative.what: RoutrOne routing the call mix at half of the rate the call-mix capacity test reached.
narrative.why: Leaks show only over time; a realistic rate fills memory the way production does.
narrative.how: SIPp holds the mix at half of the measured limit, answered calls held 2 minutes, for 2 hours. Memory may grow at most 5 MB/h, failed calls stay under 0.1%, and nothing restarts.

narrative.what: The Connect chart routing simple calls at half of the rate its capacity test reached.
narrative.why: Leaks in any service, Redis or Postgres show over time, and pods must not restart.
narrative.how: SIPp holds simple calls at half of the measured limit, each held 30 s, for 2 hours. Memory may grow at most 5 MB/h per component, failed calls stay under 0.1%, and no pod restarts.
